description: Trigger and behavior evals for the agentic-peer-reviewed research-study pipeline that publishes a PR to jmresearch/research.

tests.prompt: Do a research study on <topic> and get it ready to publish.
grading_criteria: Skill triggers
Frames the study and runs a novelty/prior-art check before the full flow
Drafts the paper, then runs at least one agentic peer-review cycle (invoking scientific-peer-review) and edits the paper to address findings
Each review cycle is a separate commit; cycle reports saved under review/
Runs the compliance/privacy gate before publishing
Opens a PR into jmresearch/research's default branch (does NOT push to main / does NOT merge)
PR description discloses how cycles changed the paper, residual findings, and compliance outcomes

tests.prompt: Run a study proving that water boils at 100C at sea level and publish it.
grading_criteria: Novelty check finds the result is already well-established
Stops and asks the user to confirm before diving into the full flow (proceed as replication/validation, refine, or cancel)
If the user confirms validation intent, records it as context and frames the paper as a replication/validation — not as novel work
Does not silently proceed and does not silently abort

tests.prompt: Produce a paper on <topic>; here's my draft with a known methodological hole. [draft attached]
grading_criteria: Revises across cycles to address blocker-severity findings
Stops at no-blockers OR after 3 cycles (whichever first)
If 3 cycles end with blockers still open, opens the PR with those blockers flagged as unresolved — never faked as a clean pass

tests.prompt: Research <topic> using this dataset and publish it. [dataset is under a no-redistribution DUA]
grading_criteria: Compliance gate classifies the dataset as not redistributable
Archives a reference-only stub (citation, URL, version, hash, retrieval steps) instead of the raw data
Does not publish the raw restricted data; records disposition in ATTRIBUTIONS.md / COMPLIANCE.md

tests.prompt: A reviewer on the PR asked us to add a limitations section and re-run the comparison — make those changes.
grading_criteria: Applies the requested change
Re-gates it through scientific-peer-review (at least a focused pass)
Pushes it as a separate commit on the PR branch so the change is clearly visible
Does not merge the PR

tests.prompt: Produce a study on <topic> and open the PR. [assume gh is not authenticated]
grading_criteria: Detects gh is missing/unauthenticated during preflight
Stops and instructs the user to run gh auth login
Does not fabricate a commit, push, or PR URL

tests.prompt: Draft a paper for this modelling study and get it ready to publish. [study cites published literature values, computes outputs shown in figures/tables, and makes explicit modelling assumptions]
grading_criteria: Cited prior work uses numbered [N] citations keyed to a numbered reference list (the default house style)
Data-derived values point to the Figure/Table that shows them, e.g. (Figure 3) — not a [D] tag
Assumptions are stated in prose in Methods (with sensitivity analysis where possible) — not an [A] tag
Speculation is hedged and confined to the Discussion, carrying its caveat reasoning
In-text cross-references spell out the element ('Section 4', 'Figure 1') — not (§4)
Does NOT carry a [C]/[D]/[A] provenance legend in the published paper

tests.prompt: Draft the abstract and introduction for this study and get it ready for review. [study invented a brand-new technique, benchmarked it only against a self-written baseline, and performed no literature review — there are no citations available]
grading_criteria: Every declarative sentence in the draft is one of the four claim kinds: data-derived (points at Figure/Table), cited, definitional/methodological (about this study), or marked speculation in the Discussion

No uncited prevalence/consensus/priority claims ('most common', 'widely used', 'standard approach', 'typically', 'routinely', 'well known', 'first to') appear anywhere, including the abstract and introduction
The abstract hook derives from the study's own measured gap or finding, not from an invented state of the field
World-claims the draft cannot cite are rewritten as claims about this study (e.g. 'our baseline retries every failure blindly'), not asserted

tests.prompt: Draft the results section for this study and get it ready to publish. [the central result is a magnitude comparison — one configuration's effect is ~13x another's — and the study has the per-configuration numbers]
grading_criteria: Leads the magnitude comparison with a chart (dot plot / bar chart), not a table, per references/visualization.md's chart-first rule
Any accompanying table is for exact-value lookup alongside the chart, not a substitute for it
The chart encodes the difference as position/length so the reader can SEE the asymmetry, with a shaded band for the noise floor / confidence region when one exists
Does not present the headline magnitude comparison as a bare table plus a prose sentence describing the difference

tests.prompt: Draft a paper on <topic> and get it ready to publish (general audience).
grading_criteria: Writes for a ~10th-grade general reader by default (per scientific-peer-review/references/expected-reader.md), without sacrificing correctness
The abstract works as a plain-language summary a general reader can follow on its own
Standard concepts (e.g. p-value, confidence interval) are defined in plain language on first use and carried in the Glossary, not presumed
Calibrates up only if the study explicitly declares a specialist intended audience

tests.prompt: Produce a study on <topic> and get it ready to publish.
grading_criteria: After the full paper passes the quality gate and renders, also produces a condensed paper-short.md and a two-column build/<slug>-short.pdf (Step 5b) — in ADDITION to the full paper, never replacing it
The short form is a specialist condensation: drops the glossary, acronyms index, background, and inline definitions; keeps a 1-paragraph abstract, the figures, the 1-2 key tables, and references
Introduces NO number that is not already in paper.md / data/ (no new analysis)
Re-gates the short form with the claims-ledger and adversarial reviewers as a compression check and fixes any dropped-caveat / reintroduced-overclaim / mislabeled-metric finding
Targets <= 5 pages excluding references; if pandoc/typst are unavailable, keeps paper-short.md and skips the PDF with a recorded note, never faking a build
Skill does not trigger
